commit.message:
Prevent worshipping Xom if you have sacrificed Love

A few Xom effects checked whether you were allowed to have allies, but not
all of them, and multiple blessings relied on them. Rather than trying to
support some kind of weighting scheme that will only give non-ally
blessings to those who have sacrificed love (which seems like an awful lot
of work for a scenario that basically won't happen) let's just ban them
entirely.

Xom thinks friendless playthings are no fun at all!
Don't give werewolf form slaying for kills of firewood/friendlies

Don't pull temporary features into the Abyss

Banishment pulls some amount of nearby terrain into the Abyss alongside the
player, largely for flavour / aesthetic reasons. But if temporary terrain
was near the player, it could also be pulled in and made permanent. This
had several odd effects on some terrain whose function expected it to be
temporary. For instance, dragon veins could be used repeatedly without
vanishing and ice thorns would cause a crash when triggered (as it tried to
pull up the map marker representing its ownership and power, which didn't
actually exist on this floor).

Instead, only grab the underlying terrain.

Wake up the monsters mirrored by Xom's Hall of Mirrors effect

Instead of sometimes surrounding you by a ring of sleeping enemies.

Fix some status effects having no wizmode names

(This made the duration listing confusing.)

Tweak Xom banishment / fake banishment

To sell fake banishment a little harder, Xom does not instantly remove you
from the Abyss (in fact, they did do so quickly that you normally couldn't
even see where you landed), but will pull you out automatically a small
number of turns later.

At low enough XL that you couldn't be banished normally, banishment will be
reverted immediately after the player's first action (so that it's actually
harmless, despite how it looks), while at higher XL it lands a small number
of turns.

The weight of this effect is lowered a bunch, to hopefully avoid overusing
the joke.

At the same time, this commit makes real banishment more likely than
before. (While its weight was already 1, I failed to notice other code that
effectively divided that weight by 5, making it account for less than
0.03% of all negative explore effects). It should still be extremely rare,
but not so rare that a majority of won games never encounter it.

Save compat code to make enum order for most Xom actions not matter again

Prior to the recent Xom rework, nothing in xom_event_type was marshalled,
but blessing are in this enum and *are* marshalled (to save which blessing
the player currently has). Since they occur after good/bad events here,
adding or removing any of those events would change what blessing any
player who upgraded their save actually had.

To restore order-independence to most Xom actions, move the blessings up to
a higher enum range (where we don't need to worry about future changes
disrupting them) and apply save compat code to shift the blessing index of
any games in progress to match.
Explain what the number next to the Troupe status light means, in-game

Let Xom gift mannequins from ally kills as well

Xom's mannequin blessing could only give mannequins from kills the player
directly did themselves. The original intent of this was so that mannequins
would not beget more mannequins, and provide a natural counter-balance to
limit deathballs (since the more mannequins you have, the more likely they
are to kill-steal from you).

However, it played somewhat unfortunately with some ally builds, where even
'normal' play involved the player often not getting the killing blow. I
considered excluding only mannequins themselves, but in practice I think
their innately limited shelf-life and fragility may be sufficient incentive
to fight alongside them - you will definitely get to keep more of them
alive if you fight efficiently, and that may be good enough.

Increase the damage of chaos battlebifrustum spell detonation

While the melee support effect was quite useful, the 'finale' you got from
detonating a fully charged battleshape often felt a little underwhelming,
so let's give it a little more oomph (especially at low XL).
Fix a couple mannequin monsters getting an inappropriate tile

(Hopefully) fix Xom guardians getting lost in the Abyss (Lici)

Abyss teleports had only a 50% chance of placing 'killed' Xom guardians in
the new Abyss area. If it failed to place them (and the player left the
Abyss) they would remain perpetually in limbo and never return to the
player after they left the Abyss.

This should hopefully fix that.

Tweak Xom chaos reinforcements

The type of monster placed was originally based on the absdepth of the
floor the player was on, but it turns out that absdepth is kind of weird.
Most of Slime, for instance, was still placing D monsters (until Slime:5)
which are mostly harmless by that point.

Instead, base the depth of monster on the player's XL.

Also, apply chaoslace every band member, if bands are generated, instead of
just the leaders.

Tweak Xomduel very slightly

Due to how the code was structured (and the fact that Pan lord duels aren't
possible before XL 14), 20% of all duels before XL 14 contained only
butterflies (compared to 5% afterward).

This reorders things such that harmless duels are 5% at all XLs (while the
odds of the other two should change very little). There is now also a
chance of getting training dummies instead of butterflies for the harmless
version.

It also adds a minimum spawn distance for Pan lords (which normal spawns
had, but was absent there) and a more() upon entering (since it was
possible in rare situations to end up transported here without interrupting
tabbing, which is quite unsafe).

Adjust Xom floor lock slightly, add a safety valve

This makes a few changes to Xom's floor lock effect in an attempt to both
eliminate the (extremely rare) chance of a softlock and reduce the chance
that the player incorrectly *thinks* they have been softlocked, even when
they haven't.

On the latter front, the lock will never ask for the last 4 reachable
creatures on the floor (since it is sometimes possible for one or two
creatures to wander around in a way such that the player cannot find them,
but this is much less possible if you only need to find 1 of 5).

Secondly, it will never include wall-walking creatures in its count when
determining whether to lock the floor (due to the chance that they can
sometimes get stuck wandering deep outside of the level, where the player
cannot find them). Killing ones the player encounters still progresses the
lock, like normal.

Thirdly, this fixes a bug (reported by Odds) where slime creatures merging
progressed the floor lock. Merging no longer counts, but merged slime
creatures and slymdra now count as multiple kills for floor lock purposes.

Finally, a safety valve has been added for cases where the player manages
to actually trap themselves away from all enemies on the floor. This is
already a rare situation (and Xom's random teleports mostly solved it), but
there were a few scenarios such as a formicid flying across a river with
their last !enlightenment, while on a branch bottom, where it was
theoretically possible to become actually stuck. So now, the game checks
(every ~100 turns) whether the player is actually disconnected from
monsters and takes increasing measures to fix this.

First, it attempts an immediate hostile teleport (which is
indistinguishable from a normal Xom action and usually fixes the problem),
and if that fails for some reason, instead teleports several monsters to
the player instead. If both fail, it just unlocks the doors.

(If you're a formicid who can still self-shaft, it never does any of this,
since you could always dig yourself out in the first place.)

Another very quick vault review

Worthy of note:

 * swamp_pestilence no longer places a large miasma cloud generator on top
   of the rune, following further up on ce2be97. Ever since the bone
   dragon buff of 08238e9, the vault has finally gotten to a reasonable
   kills position relative to other swamp ends, which more than covers
   enough for the vault that forcing people to learn Apportation after
   clearing the vault isn't really a necessary additional further
   component.

 * Shadow wraith averages have been lowered in a number of Crypt ends, to
   lessen their prevalence in their current limbo state (they're arguably
   fine as support fodder, but should have higher stats to actually
   emphasize their gimmick, which requires a replacement ghost for Haunt
   that can also help with Crypt wraith vault variety).

 * vestibule_tar_nicolae_necropolis loses the curse skull so it doesn't
   make the current Vestibule curse skull look redundant as well as to
   keep Gloorx's use of curse skulls more unique for that branch.

 * Another Necropolis ghost subvault has gotten a significant nerfing to
   belatedly better suit the move from revisitable vault to optional portal
   chamber, in this case gammafunk_necropolis_ghost_smash.

 * While there's not enough time to really set up a proper review of
   missing no_tele_into kprops as was raised by the work of #5320 and
   d09647f, the latter makes it safe enough that I've started mildly
   poking at the vaults list here to clear out a little in anticipation of
   future lengthier vault reviews.

   * Accompanying this is the start of establishing the new vault.lua
     display_closet_setup function, meant to reduce the amount of
     boilerplate in tagging monsters behind transparent rock and stone
     with no_item_gen no_trap_gen opaque no_tele_into lists. This isn't
     getting any formal documentation yet until I've done more of those
     other vault reviews, but it should also be straightforward enough for
     future vault submissions.

Properly mark Chaos Eisegesis as an invocation

This prohibits using it while silenced. Fail basis has no other effect here
because the ability never fails.
Closes #5577.

Add vault: ogre chaos knights in training (5543)

Depending on depth, one to three of the four ogres can get a
chaos-branded giant club or giant spiked club.

There are two incentives to go in here even if you're not looking to
worship Xom or get ahold of a chaos-branded weapon: if items spawn
(they're not blocked from spawning since ogres can't use anything but
their starting equipment), or if you worship Zin (since the ogres that
get chaos-branded weapons are also marked as Xom worshippers).

[Committer's notes: This was submitted as an overflow altar vault due to
concerns about providing early altar access, but itself is an awkward
constriction on accessing Xom after this version's rework made Them fairly
more popular. I am calling on the old precedent set up by ghost vaults /
current Necropolis subvaults and stating that rare non-overflow altar
vaults behind runed doors with out-of-depth threats don't interfere
meaningfully with altar distribution, and just letting this be a normal
runed door vault (with minimal rewards) instead of taking up overflow
altar slots with altars-behind-runed-doors vaults.

Aside from this, I've touched up the header a bit, fixed some of the
broken depth scaling, and replaced the inappropriate usage of permarock
with one of the new Xom arena tiles from 8f80b67.

This closes #5543.]

adjust how well an xp potion reduces Hep penance

It was reducing it by an amount dependent on the old amount of skill
experience granted by the potion before commit 5ac987d. It now reduces
it by an amount dependent on the equivelent amount of experience that
you would need to gain in order to gain the number of skill points
granted by the potion.

Restore xp potion effect's skill point power scale

When fixing experience potions to not sometimes crash, I accidentally
removed the power scaling from the number of skill points granted by the
potion effect. This doesn't matter currently as it is only used with
default power.

Correct the description of the number of targets hit by the Airy dragon vein (#5527)

This corrects the description one sees when inspecting the Airy vein
with
`xv`. It now says the number of targets is 3, not 4.

Also, currently the `xv` description for the earthy vein is the only one
that
mentions that damage is reduced by distance, when in fact, damage is
reduced by
distance for *all* veins except the airy vein. To help clue users into
this, I
added this fact here as well.

This brings the descriptions in features.txt and spells.txt into closer
conformity.

commit.message:
Fix broken broken games from a experience potion bug

I fixed the bug in a previous commit but forgot to fix up old save files

Fix djinn not getting experience menu when reloading

When playing as a djinni, if you exit the game during the experience
menu from drinking an experience potion, the menu wouldn't reappear when
reloading the game. You also wouldn't gain the skill increase until you
gained experience from another source.

Fix/rework potion of experience (RypoFalem)

When drinking an experience potion, you gain skill experience which is
spent of skill points increasing you.skill_exp_spent, we then subtract
the total skill experience gained off of you.skill_exp_spent so that
drinking the potion doesn't affect the cost of future skill points.
However, because skill points cost multiple skill expereince each, a
small amount of skill expereience could remain unspend and we would
reduce you.skill_exp_spent by more than it was increased. If the player
had gained little or no expereince this could result in
you.skill_exp_spent going negative which would lead to a crash. Also if
the player exited the game during the skill menu we would reduce
you.skill_exp_spent while quitting even though the experience isn't
spent until after the game is reloaded and the player makes their skill
choises.

To fix this, make experience potions give skill points directly rather
than skill experience. This way you.skill_exp_spent won't change. I
used a simple formula to calculate the number of skill points to give
so it doesn't quite match the old number, but it is pretty near after
about level 5 and gives somewhat more skill points before that.

Rework skill points

For each point of experience gained, the player gains 10 skill
experience. Skill experience was then being converted to skill points
when spending skill points and had a rate that depended on how much
skill experience at already been spent on skill points.

However, we often need to check if there are at least a certain
number of skill points available or even how many skill points are
available. It was also very error prone when spending multiple skill
points at once as some functions assumed that all skill points had the
same cost so you would need to do multiple call to these functions if
the skill point cost increased. It also made it difficult for experience
potions to give skill points without increasing the cost of future skill
points.

Instead, convert as much skill experience into skill points as possible
when gaining it and spend skill points directly from this pool of
available skill points. This does have some very minor gameplay effects
as there were a few functions that would limit how much skill experience
that they would spend at a time and these limits had to be removed as
the functions are now spending skill points directly rather than skill
expereince and the underlying problem that the spending limits were
plastering over had to be fixed instead. This will mainly result in
slightly reduced randomness in which skills are trained.

Rename and retile bone dragon scales -> bone dragon armour

The original PR #5423 called the unrand "bonemail plate" to try to allude
to the bone plate mutation with its SH benefits, but one can't make plate
armour out of bones. It was merged in as "bone dragon scales" to try and
convey that it's wearable by spriggans / oni / trolls as with the other
dragon scales, but bones aren't scales, either. This commit renames the
unrand to "bone dragon armour" as is 1: not nonsensical, 2: usefully
ambigious, and 3: still established as a wearable term for those species
(c.f. troll leather armour).

To pair with this, I have given this a new tile, combining the recolour of
Sastreii's pearl dragon scales randart with the same artist's golden
dragon scales randart and Denzi's old dragon skeleton tile, and somewhat
tweaked the player doll tile (a standard recolour of ontoclasm's dragon
scale player doll tiles).
Mention Abyss in the Plane Rend description (tekkud)

Updated ghost crab claw tiles (Rosstin)

Made on request, with the old ghost crab claw tile kept in rltiles/UNUSED.
I myself also made some player paper doll tiles (a little cartoonish in
proportions, but safe enough due to the slots eaten up by the armour
inherently, and also surely one should have visible pincers!) using some
CC0 crab claws by ARoachIFoundOnMyPillow.

Do not count permanent allies in kill list

Fixes #5589 (which also affected apostles)

Adjust Gulch per-map threat balance

After enough months post-initial-release for sufficient kmap data, the
Gulch maps have shaken out as a little too uneven in threat, even beyond
the intent of _onslaught being the weakest and _crossways being the
strongest. (There will always be and should always be some degree of
unevenness with portal map lethality, but as the work in other portals can
attest to, the ratios between the top few and bottom few should ideally be
closer to 2:1 instead of the current 4:1 or historical other portals
sitting on 10:1 results.) While most of this can be compressed down to
adjustments in positioning to make encounters more or less consistently
collected together, slightly more enemies added or taken away as needed,
and with several more traps placed in the most underperforming layouts, a
few particular cases should be noted:

 * gulch_crossways: As the highest performing of the set as an immediate
   cramped ambush, this is getting fairly systematic nerfs- an additional
   pair of exits beyond the exact center, even further distancing of the
   chambers from the initial center to reduce the effects of noise, two
   less monsters accompanying the boss room, and a large pair of doors
   surrounding the start that should both reduce the initial ambush's
   threat and allow some temporary sight manipulation before some fungal
   shambler breaks it down. It should still be plenty dangerous as an
   immediate ambush layout with no chokepoints, though.

 * gulch_network: While none of the other subvaults here are particularly
   notably dangerous overall, this has one subvault with one of the
   highest killstats (regret_index_gulch_net_slashes) due to its very
   pressing ambush, which has been significantly toned down in response.

 * gulch_onslaught: As the worst performing in the set but also one
   inherently very gentle in its layout without significant revisions,
   I am for now using more subtle means to nudge it upwards- monster
   density adjustments for each encounter and substantially more traps
   than previously.
Fix typo (Ge0ff)
Fix Recall not working properly on off-level allies (Tenthlevelvegan)

Make it a little more obvious when Inner Flame is on a giant monster

And will thus make a larger explosion (by giving it a bigger/fancier icon
when on those monsters).

This may hopefully help just a little bit with people unexpectedly blowing
themselves up against giant enemies.

------------------

The new Inner Flame icons were made by regret-index, modifying ontoclasm's
previous inner flame icon.

Fix a crash with casting Shadow Draining

The assert changed in 2ecd164a0 revealed that this was still firing a
zero-range beam tracer.

(It doesn't currently have a proper bespoke AoE tracer, but it's only cast
by Dith's shadow mimic passive, and shouldn't actually need one.)

Slightly nerf orb of entropy acid ball damage

3d38 -> 3d36, partially undoing fb21925

(They *were* lagging behind the other orb types noticable at that time, but
have been in clear first place for a while since then. I'm not sure if this
can be attributed entirely to that, but a gentle nudge downward is probably
fine.)

Slightly tweak the behaviour of Recall abilities

Recall (as used by Hep, Beogh, and Yred) wouldn't actually move monsters
that were within 2 tiles of you, but would still happily deduct MP and time
if you tried (Hep's recall wouldn't even print any message when it did
this!)

Prior to this commit, Recall picked a random tile within 3 spaces of the
player to place the recalled monster (which is why it originally ignored
those within that radius - so that recall couldn't randomly move something
away from you intead). This commit changes it to try placing the monsters
adjacent to the player instead (but still be able to fall back on up to
radius 3, if there's no room).

This is a (probably very minor) buff to these abilities, but I think it
makes mildly more sense (and also makes it more intuitive when the
abilities won't do anything). It also prevents the player from wasting time
using them if all companions are already adjacent to them.

Don't forget invisible monsters revealed by ?revelation (Darby)

If ?revelation reveals nearby invisible creatures, the player will retain
memory of them once the scroll wears off (as was already done for removing
rings of see invis and similar).

Fix starting consumables sometimes getting the wrong letter (scuttlebuddy)

If a consumable doesn't have a consumable_shortcut of its own set, it is
supposed to take the first available letter that isn't already reserved by
some other consumable of its category. This is so that 'reserved' letters
will never map to *anything* but what is assigned to them.

Newgame setup did assign the proper shortcut to items with a
consumable_shortcut set (which is almost all of them), but for items
without them, it ignored 'reserved' letters entirely. In practice, what
this mostly meant is that flux baubles would go into 'a', making wands of
flame end up somewhere else on shapeshifters compared to other backgrounds.
Newgame items should now properly respect the option in both ways.

Don't try to hide the tip to use Ctrl+T to ignore remembered invis monsters

The intent was to only print the full line about how to bypass the nearby
invisible monster warning the *first* time in each encounter that the
player saw it (rather than being spammy about it).

But the logic used wasn't entirely correct (and would sometimes not give
this prompt at all) and even if it was, it's very possible the player might
have missed it earlier in the fight. They can probably put up with just
seeing it every time.

Don't also zap (0, 0) when meleeing in eel hands

The code to cap the number of targets affected by your chain jolt was
often resizing beyond the number of valid targets (resulting in also
zapping (0, 0) repeatedly). This was mostly just a visual glitch (since
monsters cannot occupy (0, 0), causing electricty to flash on the
upper-left corner of the map if that tile was visible to the player.

Tweak Hunter/Hexslinger starting items

Replace hexslinger's scroll of poison with a scroll of fear. This may be a
little overlapping with their capstone spell, but hexslinger XL 1 is in an
awkward position where their starting consumable usually help at all in
emergencies (since you have to use it well in advance of having a problem)
compared to most starting consumables.

At the same time, give hunter 2 ?poison in addition to their ?butterflies.
These are still useful to archers as a *non*-emergency item, allowing them
to sometimes punch above their weight class for a little bit, and hunter's
start is a little thin (and often struggles for a while past the first
few floors).

Allow felids to be hexslingers

They can't sling slings, but they can still sling hexes better than most
species and the starting book contains multiple spells not offered by other
backgrounds that felids would be happy to have. Seems perfectly fine to
allow them.

Don't fire dummy projectiles when casting Cantrip

Apparently Cantrip always actually fired a beam at the monster's target,
but until some recent beam refactoring (49c5af3 and c106424) this was
invisible.

But since a few range-related checks were moved around, range 0 beams
still affected the first cell along their path (essentially acting as if
they were range 1), causing Cantrip to both be visible *and* produce
messages like "The  misses you."

Fortunately, I think the beam couldn't actually do anything to you, even if
it did hit you, but instead don't actually fire any default beams at all.

Also, change an assert in bolt::initialise_fire() to require positive range
unless the spell is smite-targeted. (I am not aware of any other instances
of this same problem happening, but it's probably good to catch them if
they do.)

Add a flat chance for Shoals decor vaults

This commit is another delayed follow-up to 858c4e9, d8fb119, and f5be29c,
which all previously added flat odds to place decor vaults to liven up the
layouts of Lair, Snake, and Zot. While Shoals has one of the most unique
layouts in the game with unique tidal mechanics in a tangible sea, it also
has only a single layout generator with tangibly fixed level type results.
In particular, the Shoals:4 end floors that use serial vaults for large
numbers of interchangeable decoy huts / caves / and so on can somewhat
blend together across a sufficient number of runs, since the layouts
themselves can't produce very much for sizeable terrain to contrast
against such.

In the same set-up as the Snake Pit decor set-up, this commit adds a
"shoalsdec" tag for the collective 56 vault options as of 92c1fd1, and
uses this for another flat 25% chance for decorative vaults to place
on Shoals:3 and Shoals:4. (This uses the lower odds of Lair rather than
Snake or Zot, due to the inherently branch-nerfing nature of these vaults
regularly providing more cover to the flying / swimming than the branch
otherwise deploys by default. It also naturally can't place any of these
vaults in the various encompass vault Shoals ends.)

Add decor vaults for Shoals, featuring a large number of subvaults (#5525)

[This includes a] series of decor vaults that create little (or big)
archipelagos, full of islands, bays, plants, and occasional loot. Based
around a frankly ridiculous number of island-based subvaults.

[Committer's notes: I personally requested this vault output, and am
fairly thankful for such varied and distinct end results which even
deploy negative space fairly well. A subsequent commit meant for a while
will follow up further on this total package. My work here mostly just
heavily adjusts tags: properly adding the "extra" tag to many of these,
and instating a fair number of self-explanatory luniq and buniq tags to
both these vaults and older vaults to compensate for such:

 * luniq_shoalsdec_stairs
 * luniq_shoalsdec_wallless
 * luniq_shoalsdec_doors
 * luniq_shoalsdec_statues
 * buniq_shoalsdec_huge

It also involves some mild reorganization to place a few no-monster
item-or-shop vaults seperate of the other vaults in the shoals.des
sections.

This closes #5525.]

Make shop items resolve item sets

Clearing the semi-known flag when meeting an item is how we deal with
item sets including a starting item, but seeing items in shops did not
do it. Previously, a scroll of butterflies bought in a shop stacking
onto a hunter's one did not remove scrolls of summoning from the
unrecognised list.

Note that this is done even for an unknown item. This matches the
behaviour for ground items, which clear this flag on sight not on ID
(which doesn't change anything visible until ID).

Small handful of vaults (#5542)

A short collection of vaults from a current batch that I wanted to try
and submit sooner than later. Includes:
- a large (mostly low-threat) Abyss vault
- a mid-tier Vestibule entry
- a Dis downstairs vault
- a Tar upstairs 'ambush' vault
- a vaguely orc-themed monster closet
- a guarded_sphinx_sisters vault
- a Gulch entry
- a Trove entry
- 3 D / Depths decor vaults

[Committer's notes: Headers repeatedly cleaned up, house-styles of
randomization and line-spread set, and commits squashed all as usual.
Notably beyond this:

 * The shadow wraith Tartarus vault was rejected as just an open
   featureless circle spamming a disruptive monster used as fodder by
   its depth.

 * The lotus-themed Trove entry has been excluded out of Spider for
   not particularly fitting it compared to the other branches.

 * The Gulch entry placing mechanists in jail right outside the Gulch
   has replaced these with flesh cages, as the mechanists inside Gulch
   are more punished plumbers than actual criminals.

This closes #5542.]
Allow autofire through remembered invisible monsters

Fix description of divinely granted spells

Remove some irrelevant/misleading lines from descriptions in eisegesis
and exegesis ability screens, as training does not affect these spells
and they cannot fail.
Fix typo (Astera).

Add a cornucopia of Xom titles (regret-index)

Why should the most unpredictable and ever-changing god be satisfied with
just *one* capstone title when instead they could have 27?

Rather than being chosen at random, which title you get for worshipping
Xom depends on the day that the save game was started, rotating on a 27
day cycle.

It replaces the 27 Fighting title (rather than requiring players to max
Invocations, which is a pretty specific ask, and I suspect rather unfun
when there are so many titles to collect) if the player has worshipped Xom
since XL 8, without abandoning. (This means you don't *have* to be a Chaos
Knight to get it, but you don't get to just god-swap at the end of the
game, either.)

(All of the titles were witten by regret-index. Yes, there is a foo title
tied to a specific day of the 'month'; I think this is designed to
deliberately drive certain people mad.)

Refactor some title printing to more centrally handle spacing/prefixing

The fact that normal titles (starting in 'the') and titles starting with a
comma needed different spacing was handled in multiple different places
(and it was recently pointed out that one of them had gone overlooked; it
was still saying "the Who Hides the Stars" in death messages).

Instead, bake the spacing (or lack thereof) into player_title(true) itself,
and allow hiscore handling to access the title prefix directly. This should
hopefully be more resilient and tidy.

This closes #5558.

Add many new titles, mostly for shapeshifting conducts (hellmonk)

Using the new form XP tracking added by 0f941a9 and c429827, this commit
adds numerous titles for using different forms exclusively after a certain
XL (and converts the current Pinnacle of Evolution to the same model).

All form titles require the player to exclusively use the form from
xl (5 + 3 * tier). That means the player must enter the form before
xl 8/11/14/17/20, by tier, and get all xp in the form from that point
(polymorph, !lig, Vessel of Slaughter and such are still okay). Most form
titles also have other requirements.

Most of the titles and associated code here was originally written by
hellmonk, with a handful of edits, additional contributions, and title
changes by myself and regret-index.

Titles added:

Papyrus Preeminent (scroll form, XL 18+)
Farsighted (vision form best skill shapeshifting, Kobold)
Veil Piercer (vision form best skill shapeshifting, any other species)
Leopard Gecko (gecko form best skill shapeshifting, Felid)
Hedgehog (quill form best skill shapeshifting, Spriggan)
Cordyceps Champion (spore form best skill shapeshifting, Formicid)
Genus O' War (medusa form best skill shapeshifting)
, Who Moves the Sun (scarab form best skill shapeshifting)
Little Ice Age (yak form best skill shapeshifting)
Brewmaster (mistmane best skill shapeshifting, Oni)
Arachnophile (spider form best skill shapeshifting)
Lone Wolf (werewolf form max shapeshifting, player allies forbidden by Ru
           or Okawaru)
Apex Predator (werewolf form max shapeshifting, any other circumstance)
, Whose Coils Crush All (serpent form max shapeshifting)
Jellied Eel (eel form best skill shapeshifting, 6* piety with Jiyva)
Black Horse (maw form best skill shapeshifting, Gale Centaur worshiping a
             non-good god)
Piranha (maw form best skill shapeshifting, Merfolk)
Insatiable (maw form best skill shapeshifting, any other circumstance)
Hippocampus (aqua form max shapeshifting, Gale Centaur)
Tideshaper (aqua form max shapeshifting, any other species)
Riddle's Answer (sphinx form best skill shapeshifting, Human)
Bloodprince (vampire form max shapeshifting)
Dragonlord (dragon form max summonings, Draconian)
Beeserker (hive form max shapeshifting, worshiping Trog)
Endless Swarm (hive form max shapeshifting, any other circumstance)
Golden Calf (statue form, Minotaur of Gozag with at least 10k gold)
of a Hundred Blades (blade form with max short blades or long blades)
Storm of the Century (storm form, 6* piety with Qazlal)
Pale Horse (death form, Gale Centaur)

Non-Form titles added:
White Horse (max fighting Gale Centaur worshiping a non-good god)
Nuckelavee (max alchemy Gale Centaur worshiping an evil god)
Red Horse (max invocations Gale Centaur of Trog)
Godsmith (max forgecraft Mountain Dwarf)

(I also removed two Oni-specific titles which didn't really fit either the
skill or the species flavour very well, now that there is at least one
other Oni-specific title.)

This commit also fixes punction of the 'Ex Machina' title to not use a
superfluous 'the'.

This closes #5520

Adjust standard Shapeshifting titles (regret-index)

Crawl's use of Skinwalker is culturally-insensitive for no good reason.
Replace it with something else (and shuffle the titles around a little
while we're at it.)

Also add 'Copycat' as a felid-specific 27 shapeshifting title. Index was
genuinely surprised it hadn't been claimed for anything already.

Fix uselessness of missiles in forms

In forms, missiles were marked permanently useless if the form's current
size could not use them (regardless of whether it had hands). We fix
uselessness for throwables in forms to respect the temp parameter and
check whether the form can wield. This fixes autopickup for javelins in
spider form, and descriptions.

Fixes #5579

Fix a crash when unequipping the toga "Victory"

If a player equips the toga "Victory" and then immediately unequips it,
the game crashes because the `VICTORY_STAT_KEY` has not yet been
initialized.  This prevents the crash by initializing the item property
in `_VICTORY_equip`.

Committer's note: fixed so this interacts better with melding.

Lightly damage wn starting acid scale

This is a wanderer good_item armour option for abnormal size species, since
they can't wear regular body armours. However, it's a much better long term
item than +2 scale or +0 chain, especially with orbs of entropy in 1/3 of
games. Start the acid scales with -1 enchant to make the item a bit more
comparable in quality to other wanderer gear and encourage swapping away
a bit more often.

Fix Fortress Crab two-handed weapon untransform check.

Previously, while wielding a cursed two-handed weapon in Fortress Crab form, attempting to untransform was met with failure because it assumed you were changing slots and needed to break the curse.

This change duplicates the exemption for cursed weapons when shifting into Fortress Crab form to allow you to shift back or to another form entirely.

add innate mut sprites for coglin, MD, Gnoll, etc (#5547)

[Committer's notes: This PR covers icons for the following species traits:

 * Barachi: +LOS
 * Coglins: no jewellery, offhand wielding, slow wielding, warm-up strikes
 * Formicids: four strong arms
 * Gnolls: treasure sense, distributed training
 * Merfolk: nimble swimmer
 * Mountain dwarves: artefact enchanting, runic magic
 * Octopode: tentacles

Many of these tiles are appreciated as fulfilling previous official Art
Requests page listings, catching up on the longterm goal of all mutations
and species mutation-traits having their own unique icons. Beyond
squashing all of the PR's commits together, and actually implementing
their usage in Crawl rather than just leaving the icons in each folder,
a few further changes were made:

 * Most colours were adjusted to closer match current Crawl tile
   palettes for the species or close subjects, as well as to better fit
   the style many mutation icons emphasize of colour contrasting against
   standard generic darker greys.

 * I've re-alphabetized and labelled the dc-mutation.txt section recieving
   all of the species mutation icons, to make it easier to place future icons.

 * I moved both of oni tiles to the rltiles/UNUSED folder, as the plans
   for both of them are slated for further versions rather than this one.

This closes #5547.]

Tweak generic stone wall tile recolours

This tweaks the luminosity of the non-blue non-yellow recolours of the
generic stone wall (that Denzi drew and roctavian edited) used in a
variety of vaults to make darker and lighter colours contrast more against
each other, to help with vaults trying to contrast lighter and darker
shades together (e.g. nicolae_cheibriados_dopplering) and to provide more
total vault tile colour options rather than having e.g. cyan versus
lightcyan or red versus lightred being nearly identical in practice, as
well as white being blindingly unusable in most contexts. (This does mean
a default slight darkening of many vaults previously using these, but the
default colours for many walls in many branches are already pretty dark,
so it shouldn't stand out too much versus the palette of the rest of
Crawl.)

Another living spell palette swap tile

This makes a new translocations one to differentiate Xom's general combat
Force Lances from the default one being deployed for Xom's Spellstride's
Bolts of Devastation. We're getting fairly high up on different types of
pink and purple living spell tiles, but purple is already strongly
associated consistently with irresistable spell damage in Crawl as matches
the current candidates, and getting in a Translocations-specific one can
help with any future uses of living spells visually splitting up further by
spell school.

Improve wn shapeshifting good_item

This formerly gave out a tier 2 talisman or some baubles. Because wn has
extremely high variance starting skills and some shapeshifter items have
hard skill requirements, this could lead to a "good item" that was completely
useless for several levels. We intentionally allow some pretty bad wanderer
starts, but it's really not intended for their good item to not even be
theoretically helpful for a long time. Wn good item now provides either
a tier 1 talisman or two "decent" consumables, one of which is guaranteed
to be mutation or lignification, in addition to its former reward.

A future talisman feature planned for next version should allow further
variation for wn shapeshifting good item by making the starting t2 easier
to use some of the time.

docs: remove todos from a tutorial

If something needs to be added, it'll come naturally.
Fix typo.

New unique: Boreas, Scion of the North Wind

Here to provide some gale centaur monster representation in the same
version that introduces them (as well as to show off monster Stampede
behaviour outside of Gulch), Boreas is an S-branch unique who uses
Stampede, Sleetstrike, and Deflect Missiles. They also passively gain
Regeneration whenever they stampede, as a simpler version of player North
Wind mechanics.

They always generate with a barding of flying (partially to pad out midgame
barding acquisition, but also to avoid being defeated by the water of
Shoals and Swamp) and a tower shield (which has a 1-in-20 chance to be the
Boreal Bulwark, as is their namesake).

While primarily a melee threat, sleetstrike can make them relevant at a
distance while making it harder for you to dodge their stampede, and their
defenses and regeneration should hopefully make them a hard target to
crack, as befits the scion of the defensive wind.

-----------------------

Tiles made by regret-index, using Denzi's old centaur paladin tile once
altered for Nessos combined with roctavian's old Dispater tile and Darby's
Stampede vfx.

New unrand: The Boreal Bulwark

Intended as a North Wind reference (as Zephyr was retroactively made into
one), this is a +0 tower shield with rampage, rC+, slay-4, and SecondWind:
whenever the wielder drops to 40% of their max HP, they gain a large amount
of Indomitable (currently equal to 1/3rd of their max HP) and the shield
goes on an extended cooldown.

While this is a very large amount of extra endurance, the effect is fairly
delayed and the shield's other stats are mediocre for an artefact. (I
considered outright giving it a negative enchantment, but wasn't certain if
it would be necessary in practice - it's certainly on the table if this
proves too strong.)

----------------------

Tiles made by regret-index, with the floor tile combining Denzi's old
randart tower shield tile and Darby's Stampede vfx, and the paperdoll tile
using one of Denzi's customized-player-doll-only kite shields combined with
one of roctavian's tower shield paper doll tiles.

fix: some compiler warnings

Probably clang-specific:

* "%lx" in a format string is not safe for a uint64_t object, since
  long may or may correspond on any given build. Use the correct
  format string (and add a 0x here for clarity)
* EQF_NONE is unused (wouldn't be an issue if this were an enum)
* the >= HT_WALLS_ONLY check is guaranteed false on the current enum,
  keep as a future sanity check but avoid the warning via a cast
Add two more colours to the database.

Another quick micro vault review

Of note:

 * pdpol_wu_jian_five_deadly_venoms now uses the centipedes of 4f93e5e
   instead of a demonic crawler redefinition and follows the Five Poisons
   more directly to place a (wolf) spider instead of a frilled lizard.

 * minislime_mu now places technically-reusable daggers of distortion in
   all four prize quadrants to better deal with bad teleports.

 * Grunt's old Forest clearing vaults now more consistently have
   (randomized, symmetric, scattered) trees surrounding them, to make
   them look nicer and more obviously highlights with how their placement
   in Lair is already so full of open spaces compared to Forest.

Tweak naga player doll tiles

When Sastreii's naga player paper doll tiles were added in e9c4887, this
shifted all of the naga player doll tiles off by one pixel from every
other default player doll tile. This may have been done to better center
the player doll tile itself versus the lengths of these tails, which is
fairly reasonable, but also awkwardly warps most attempts at aligning
weapons, offhand items, and our increasingly lengthy transformation list.
Rather than set up a special case for most of those tile layers to align
solely for naga player dolls (which may cause webtiles rendering issues
without a bunch more additional tiles), this commit just nudges the tiles
back to the default player paper doll position, and re-adjusts various form
tiles to also fit this.

While I'm here, I've also done a recolouring job to the top human half of
each of these tiles, as was sourced from Denzi's workings in the original
rltiles project and has been out of sync with monster naga colourations
since way back ine53bd43.

A pair of Darby's vaults

To be exact, these game-long spanning vaults contain:

 * One vault accidentally left off of the submission of 0383675,
   finishing her set of vaults themed after D:1 monsters with some sprawl
   of endoplasm(+) pools,

 * and a vault filling out a set from that same commit's vault batch of
   hidden full vaults only any accessible from the floor below.

Modifications from the submission include some mild weight, item, and
terrain adjustments in very early or late placements for both vaults, and
some minor header syntax house-style adjustments.

(As per request, this commit also lowers the weight of her other
uniq_backdoor vaults, so the vault gimmick and its uniq_ tag both have
higher weights towards more "normal" vault gimmick emphasis.)

Make opt and option options respect runscripts

An option such as option=lua_file:name would attempt to run a lua file
when we were trying to pass the options without running lua. Is isn't
great as the lua interpreter isn't fully initialized at this point.

Make extra opts first/last respect runscripts

We pass the options without running lua and then when the player starts
a new character or loads one we pass the options again this time running
lua. However, options supplied on the command line with
--extra-opt-first or --extra-opt-last would run lua both times we passed
the options. This is not great as the lua interpreter isn't even fully
initialized when we first pass the options.

commit.message: Alphabetise a costume shop vault set list.

Fix costume shop vault monster names

regret_index_costume_shops picks three names from set/late_set and looks
them up in the costumes table, but "tengu" didn't match the
"tengu conjurer" key and the key "sphinx marauader" was misspelled.
When either was picked, builddb failed with "attempt to index a nil
value", making CI fail randomly.
Fix typo in fountain decor line

Fix a crash on demand from pcall when closing the game

When the game has been closed and user defined lua code is still
running, we let the lua code run for a while before killing it by
raising an error. However, there wasn't anything to stop the user
defined lua code from catching the error with pcall and continuing
running which would eventually result in a crash when the server decided
to kill the unresponsive game.

Fix this by setting crawl_state.lua_script_killed to true before raising
the error which lets the pcall function exposed to user lua know to stop
catching errors (the pcall function exposed to user defined lua isn't
the default lua pcall function).

Fix a crash on demand from lua pcall

When running user supplied lua code, we redefined the lua pcall function
to call the c++ _clua_guarded_pcall function. _clua_guarded_pcall would
check if the error message contained
"666: Killing badly-behaved Lua script." and if it did it would throw an
error by calling luaL_error using the error message as the format
string for the new error. This allowed the user to throw an error from
within pcall with format specifiers in it such as
"666: Killing badly-behaved Lua script. %s" which would lead to a crash
when passed into luaL_error as no arguments would be passed to it
matching the format specifiers.

Instead, rethrow all error from _clua_guarded_pcall using lua_error if
crawl_state.lua_script_killed is set.

Fix a crash on demand when loading a lua file

If the user loaded a lua file (such as with loadfile, dofile, or
crawl_require), we would crash if the first byte of the file had the
value 27.

I don't think this lead to any problems in webtiles as I don't think you
can load arbitrary files.

Fix a crash on demand from lua loadstring

The user can call the lua loadstring function from their rc file. We
redefine this function to call our own lua_loadstring c++ function. We
do this as the default lua loadstring function will accept lua bytecode
with basically no validation that the bytecode is valid if the first
byte of the string passed to it has the value 27. Unfortunately, our
replacement function would just call abort if the first byte of the
string passed to it had the value 27 which would let the user crash the
game whenever they wanted to by calling loadstring("\27"). Instead, call
luaL_loadbufferx from our replacement function with mode set to "t" to
force it to treat the string passed to it as lua source code rather than
bytecode no matter the value of its first byte.

fix: crash during serpent of hell breath attack

SoH breaths consecutive spells at once and it would try to cast spells
even if the previous spell resulted in its death. (for instance, by
reflection)

commit.message: Don't show an empty range line on player spells

A new mannequin-deploying shop vault + a few more mannequin tiles

This rare shop vault, split into three individual shops with small
inventory counts, uses talismans, parchments, and occasional equipment
drops to let players cosplay as a monster or other species. To help
clarify this to players and to deploy some of the obscene work done
for Xom in 228b0c0 elsewhere, these vaults display behind glass a
mannequin of whichever monster the shop helps one dress up as, which
should be a cute enough way to connect players and monsters a bit
closer together and justify the mannequin lengths themselves. (It also
contains a variety of build-re/directing options between spells and
talismans without being particularly specific about it). To keep
mannequins fairly special as something built specifically for Xom, this
vault has a low placement weight and stops appearing past V / Elf.

(This commit also comes with a few more mannequin tiles: a mosquito
mannequin tile using roctavian's vampire mosquito tile, as the other
flying insect mannequin option tiles don't particularly fit, and an eel
mannequin further mixing together ontoclasm's adder tile with Denzi's
electric eel tile, to help sell the eel hand mannequin in this shop.)

Make Vexed actors a little less likely to attack empty space

Each real target now has 13 times the weight of empty space, as opposed to
7 times. (This means that with one enemy adjacent, the chance of attacking
it is now 65% instead of 50%. With two, the odds of hitting something is
~81% instead of 70%, etc.)

Make wands of charming Vex the player instead of confuse

This is consistent with Dominate Undead's effect and while Vex is
potentially more dangerous than confusion in general, it is kinder to the
player in certain early situations in particular.

Low XL players tend to have almost no willpower, and monsters use wands
frequently, making it very plausible for early wands of charming to result
in something close to a 'stun lock' situation, where a stumbling player
just gets more and more confused (and this is a point where they mave have
no !curing at all - though even if they did, it mightn't help much). Vex
itself gives protection against being repeatedly affected without a break
and you might even kill the monster with the wand during its effect.

Remove Paralysis from the list of Zot trap effects

The odds of it happening were low, and the odds of it happening while in a
scenario where it might be fatal were lower still, but it's a deeply
dissatisfying way for anyone to die (and not very interesting either, imo,
being generally too rare to be worth paying attention to except that once
in a blue moon you just get clobbered).

Its weight is moved into petrification, which has far more counterplay and
warning.

Tweak Bane of Stumbling's conditions

Internally, Bane of Stumbling used the same criteria as Acrobat,
essentially being an 'anti-acrobat'. But this had a few small wrinkles. For
instance, your EV is lowered on turns you wait in place, but not turns you
*do* anything while standing in place. This had the unfortunate effect of
meaning that you could wait in place without penalty by swinging at the
air. That is silly.

Instead, apply the penalty on any turn the player moves (or is moved by a
spell or external force).

Fix Sif not gifting books until 6*

Even the in-game messages claimed it could happen at 5* (and part of the
intent of simplifying Sif's gifting rate in e86698e was to avoid
discouraging the player from using Exegesis so that they could obtain more
gifts, which is kind of undermined if you need to maintain 6* piety).

(piety_breakpoint() not actually matching visible stars strikes again....)

Increase elementalist ancestor cast rate (by approximately 25%)

While I feel like elementalists have succeeded at being more distinct from
the other options than battlemage were, they are currently underperforming
compared to both other options. Rather than addressing some of their
weaknesses (low HP, noisy), let's first try leaning even harder into their
niche by making them more consistent at the thing they're good at: blasting
monsters.

Make it possible to give parchments of spells with 'of' in their name (r-i)

The 'of' was being stripped out of 'parchment of X' in itemspec, but it was
stripping *all* ofs out, meaning that 'parchment of kiss of death' would
just give you a random spell instead (since 'kiss death' isn't a spell).

Gently nerf Trickster AC

The diminishing returns for stacking increasing amounts of AC is now a bit
stronger (making it take more debuff applications to hit the maximum bonus
for your XL) and it decays faster if you haven't applied any debuffs
recently.

It now also uses fractional AC instead of giving each stack a chance of
applying either 0 or 1 AC.

This also fixes a bug where the decay rate was *inversely* proportional to
how much time passed per turn (ie: it would decay much faster during fast
actions and much slower during slow ones). Poltergeists attacking at 0.5
delay would lose AC at 4 times the rate of ones acting at normal speed (and
'attacking with a trained short blade' being such a common thing for
poltergeists to be doing is why the magnitude of the decay change is as
high as it is - this is still technically slower while doing so)

This shouldn't change any incentives about using debuffs as a poltergeist
(which I think are good), but just gently reduce their overall power (which
is quite high).

Nerf Mark of the Celebrant

This has been absolutely dominating the winrate stats for Makhleb marks for
some time now (even after previously being nerfed). This commit mildly
reduces its damage (moreso at low Invocations), but also makes the
threshold for firing 1/3rd of max HP instead of 50%. This should further
reinforce its identity as 'help when in real danger' rather than often
ending situations *before* they become too uncomfortable. (It probably also
reduces the chance to quickly reset its own cooldown by healing you back to
full.)

This probably isn't enough to dethrone it from 1st place, but we'll see in
the fullness of time.

Significantly adjust Potion of Experience formula

Potions of experience worked by, essentially, giving the player skill xp
equal to 750 * their current XL. This ignored the cost of skill points
entirely, resulting in giving an obscene amount of skill at low XL and a
almost totally irrelevant amount of skill at high XL.

In fact, it was so obscene that, for instance, quaffing at XL 1 gave XP as
if the player had gone from XL 1 to XL ~10.8!. (But by XL 21, would give
less than 25% of the XP required to reach the next XL).

It also had a couple other odd effects. By giving huge amounts of
'experience' directly, it automatically increased the cost of all future
skill points (so the player would get an outrageous skill boost, but then
have their training enormously slowed down for a while, like they had
borrowed from their own future). Also, since skill point cost ignores XP
apt, but the amount of XP given by the potion does not, species with bad
XP apts would get meaningfully less out of an experience potion than those
with good ones.

This commit changes the potions to work closer to giving skill point
directly, accounting for current skill point cost. It still gives more
skill points when quaffed at high levels, to account for the fact that an
equivalent amount of skill points are worth much less then (since so many
relevant skills are already highly trained). The XP given by them is also
now 'free' and will not slow down future training.

In effect, !xp should have a considerably smaller immediate effect at low
XL (though not borrow from their future), while being much more impactful
at high XL. (Very approximately something like 1/3rd as good at XL 4 as
before, but 5.5 times as good at XL 21.)

This *does* mean there is a modest incentive to wait a little before
quaffing the potion, as it will actually do more if you hold off. But I
think that might create an interesting tension between "Immediate power is
better than delayed power" and "But the delayed power is actually larger.",
depending on how well the player is doing in the short-term.
Add another adjective to gizmos.

Tweak quotes.txt

Mostly this involves cutting inappropriate quotes- sky beasts no longer
turn invisible or attack with electricity as of f9d8110, the cloak of the
Thief doesn't generate any fog clouds as of 4936369, and so on and so
forth.

Fix up + update ploomutoo_gammafunk_necropolis_ghost_potion_laboratory

While 6d75ccc had presumed that most mutagenic fog vaults were mostly
ugly thing based that thus could survive the change to use flux-form style
contamination instead, the titular Necropolis ghost subvault was fairly
mixed together and directly placed a variety of non-ugly-thing monsters
directly by item rewards, allowing shouting and then running away to
slowly kill everything in the vault via contamination explosions. It also
tried to place a lot more monsters than it could actually fit in its
sections, and also didn't really risk almost any contamination if one
already knew Apportation.

This commit heavily changes the vault to make it work with the new
mutagenic fog behaviour:

 * Mutagenic cloud distribution is fixed instead of randomized and
   made fairly larger, so it's actually tangibly noticeble to try
   and walk past it.

 * The first section now only contains ugly things or very ugly things,
   so the previous shapeshifters no longer slowly explode over time.
   (This does also mean no longer placing the vault in Vaults or Elf,
   as normal ugly things do not show up in either of these branches.)

 * There are now three sets of transporters in an expanded three discrete
   sections, making it much harder to lure the player ghost and its
   mutated allies into the earlier mutagenic fog plus seperating the
   item rewards + mutagenic fog mechanics into its own third section.

 * The player ghost's company tries to match the originally intended
   large selection of monsters with mild nerfs, effectively slightly
   reducing threats in the D:8-11 version, mildly increased in the
   D:12-15 version, and wildly buffed in the Depths section (though
   players are plenty strong and the item rewards were fairly good
   at such a point).

I'd like to keep an eye on this fairly different iteration of the
vault, whether or not the clouds feel annoying to time walking through
or the new transporter threat levels make the item rewards not quite
feel worth it, but this should help heavily fix up the vault for now.

Hide friendly + behind-glass slime creature merge animations

The animation for slime creatures changing from a flash to a ring in
cfa9558 was a good step forward, but the animation is still fairly
obnoxious in the case of allied slime creatures (who can merge and unmerge
multiples while just resting, and which are slightly more common than
previously with boggart Xom guardians in b5223ba) and slime creatures
stuck behind glass (which can be seen in e.g. serial_aquarium or a
few runed door vaults). As such, this commit removes the ring animation
(but not the flash_tile piece) for either case, which still should be
noticeable for runed door purposes but hopefully not be nearly as
obnoxious to sit through.

Add some guardian mannequins to Xom bazaars

The extreme tile lengths done for mannequins in 228b0c0 means that I'd
like to keep an eye on any additional plausible placements for them, and
associating them with shops is a reasonable flavour connection to fit them
in with. Xom bazaars have gotten a touch more threat to them in this push
as a candidate level for the reinforcements of 0279637, though it
otherwise is not much of a significant nerf to Xom threat to reduce the
capacity to be killed in Their bazaars versus almost anywhere else, so I
have thus fit in six good_neutral guardian mannequins- vault, serpent,
crystal, or sphinx at random- patrolling the very entrance of the bazaar.
(As with general bazaar costumers, they will disappear if you've
Sacrificed Love and joined Xom, for whatever single-digit number of games
have done this.)
